summary.name: Animated Reaction Captions (Motion Design and Cinematography; supplemental, user-requested direction). Explicit: a descriptive reaction-text broadcast treatment, distinct from continuous subtitles or general kinetic typography.
summary.visualIdentity: Explicit: concise emphasis text in expressive display lettering, with consistent layered outlines, shadows, reaction stickers and small doodles. Each emotion has a distinct color and motion signature. Three emotion treatments are an optional example, not a requirement. Inferred: suits playful, expressive, vertical-first commentary.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: short emphasis words that react to moments or verbal stress, with 9:16 framing as an optional example. Inferred: vertical shorts, reaction-driven commentary and highlight reels with few spoken lines. Unspecified: formal, corporate or long-form content, which the source does not address.
summary.limitations: Explicit: captions must keep faces, dialogue subtitles and platform overlays unobstructed. Reading holds take priority over beat density, and captions must not pop on every beat. Two-color contrast checks do not verify text over footage, so representative frames need inspection. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production.
summary.palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #FFF5E5 for layout, foreground #282E3B for text and outlines, and accents #DA855C, #668FA3 and #A47CA3 assigned once to selected emotions. Foreground on background (12.592) and accent_1 with foreground (4.851) meet normal-text targets. Accent_2 and accent_3 (about 3.9) are decorative only. Gradients are disabled; supplied colors override these tokens.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Explicit: short spring entrances, squash, bounce and wobble timed to reactions or verbal stress, followed by readable holds. Motion must derive from seekable composition time, with no live interaction in video. Motion-037 (phrase scatter and step-in) is optional and only if scene assets support it. Inferred: HTML delivery should drop bounce under reduced motion.
summary.audio: Unspecified by the style; the audio direction is a proposal framework. Options include music, voiceover, sung vocals, effects, ambience or silence, chosen per topic and stated as assumptions. Explicit: beat-timed entrances apply only to a supplied soundtrack, not speech. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals, and never invent audio assets.
summary.assetRequirements: Actual display fonts, loaded locally before rendering. Reaction stickers and small doodles as approved or authorized assets. Exact caption copy supplied by the task; do not invent copy or brand marks. Inferred: footage or scene illustration is needed for safe-area checks. Missing assets must be reported, not silently replaced.
summary.combinations: Explicit: reaction captions are usually best used alone, since they already include doodles, stickers and squash motion. Suggested: style-105 as a timing system that cues entrances to a supplied soundtrack's beats. Keep emotion colors and reading holds, avoid beat-reactive colors outside the palette, and treat motion-037 as optional only.
summary.productionApproach: Explicit: HyperFrames is the default composition and export pipeline, and Remotion is a fallback only for a verified, recorded limitation. HTML/CSS and SVG handle lettering, outlines and shadows. Rough.js is optional for doodles and emphasis circles, and mo.js for optional bursts. A paused GSAP timeline drives motion. Verify forward, backward and direct seeks, and inspect safe areas.
